what: Consolidated Edison delivers electricity, gas and steam to New York City and Westchester County. It does not generate most of the power: it owns the wires, pipes and the steam system that heats much of Manhattan.
customers: About 3.5 million electricity customers and over a million gas customers in New York City and the surrounding area.
money: electricity delivery in New York City and Westchester
gas distribution and the Manhattan steam system
a neighbouring utility and transmission projects
moat: A legal monopoly over the energy networks of the densest city in the United States, where building anything competing is impossible.
risks: Debt of about $26 billion against almost no cash
New York regulators set the returns it may earn and have pushed back on rate requests
Underground work in New York City is extremely expensive
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: New York's electrification targets require very large network investment, which raises the base it earns a return on
A dividend raised every year for five decades
watch: Rate case outcomes in New York and the approved return on equity.
